themes: The Quran revealed on a blessed night
summary_for_children: Ad-Dukhan means The Smoke. It says the Quran was sent down on a blessed night and tells how Pharaoh's people left behind gardens and springs when Allah saved the Children of Israel.
world_title: The Still Sea and Abandoned Gardens
environment_concept: A calm blessed night (44:3), a sea lying still (44:24) and gardens and springs left behind (44:25).
architecture_and_scenery: Night sky, a stilled sea, gardens and springs left empty, noble dwellings and fields.

palette.lighting: Night, then grey smoky light, then calm

activities.name: What stays
activities.description: Find what was left behind and talk about what really lasts (adaptation).
activities.label: artistic educational adaptation, not an event in the Quran

activities.name: Night of the Quran
activities.description: Light the night sky by reading 44:3.
activities.label: artistic educational adaptation, not an event in the Quran

activities.name: Gardens and springs
activities.description: Find four fruits still lying in the empty gardens.
activities.label: artistic educational adaptation, not an event in the Quran

narration_plan: No people shown; narration focuses on what lasts.

depiction_rules: No prophet, person or representation of Allah is shown. Unseen realities are never pictured. Interactive activities are labelled as adaptations.

primary_mechanic.text: Count the gardens, springs and fine places a proud people left behind (44:25-27), as a quiet survey.

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Warning of the Smoke
story_library.children_narration: Surah Ad-Dukhan contains powerful warnings, including the image of smoke, and reminds us of Pharaoh's people and the rescue of the Children of Israel. The message encourages people to take guidance seriously before the opportunity passes.

world_idea.title: The Valley of Warnings
world_idea.description: Explore an atmospheric landscape with shifting mist, then follow a narrated historical journey through an Egyptian setting and a sea-crossing sequence. Avoid presenting the speculative appearance of the smoke as historical fact.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
story_library.rule_conflicts_resolved: The smoke (44:10) is not pictured, and the mist in the world is not presented as that smoke.
